the intentional transfer of bivalve species for aquaculation purposes is one of many vectors for the introduction, establishment and spread of non-native species around the world; that the European Union (EU) has developed a legal framework to minimize the effects of the introduction and transfer of non-native species; and that there is a need for a more integrated and holistic approach to risk assessments for transfer activities.
the transfer of species for the aquaculture purpose has been a common practice in the European Atlantic region for a long time.

the development of a comprehensive risk analysis framework for bivalve transfer for aquaculture.
the identification and analysis of transfer activities and their potential impacts on the marine environment, and the development of a framework for the risk assessment of such activities.
the identification of potential threats and risks due to transfer activities and the implementation of measures to minimize the negative impacts on the environment and the economy.

the existing legal framework does not provide sufficient protection of the marine environment from the effects of bivalve transfers, as the framework is not sufficiently harmonized.
the existing legal framework is not sufficient to protect marine ecosystems from the introduction of exotic bivalve species.
there is no evidence of negative impacts of transfers of bivalves on the environment.

the existing legal frameworks are insufficient to prevent the introduction of new species in Europe and to minimize the negative impact of transfer activities in Europe.
transfer activities are not only an important economic activity but also a potential risk to the environment.

the existing legislation does not sufficiently address the risks associated with transfer activities of benthic invertebrates.
